linkedin.title: This Week in Finance & Tech
linkedin.body:
It has been a busy week for tech and science. Here is the latest on what is moving the needle.

Hardware prices are on the rise. A shortage of memory chips and key components has led to a £100 price increase across Apple's iPhone lineup. Meanwhile, Apple is also facing a $250 million settlement regarding claims that it failed to deliver on promised AI upgrades for Siri. If you bought an iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, or any iPhone 16 model in the US since June 10, 2024, you may be eligible to file a claim.

In other product news, Meta is moving away from cameras with its latest AI glasses. These new models focus on being lighter and offer up to 12 hours of battery life. Browsers are also seeing shifts as Firefox 156 launches alongside a growing ecosystem of alternative browsers like LibreWolf and Waterfox for users who want different features.

Looking at space and science, SpaceX has scheduled the 14th test flight for Starship on September 28. This mission aims to have the craft orbit Earth multiple times over a 10-hour period. In lunar news, NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter has captured images of a 728-foot impact crater on the moon, a rare event that typically happens only once a century.

On the sustainability front, Barber’s Farmhouse Cheesemakers in the UK is using a clever heat pump system. They are now drawing heat from fresh milk to boil water, significantly cutting their carbon emissions. Researchers have also made progress in neuroscience, identifying rare brain cells that appear to be responsible for triggering sleep.

instagram.title: NASA is studying astronaut health on Crew-13

slides.headline: NASA is studying astronaut health on Crew-13
slides.subtitle: The mission includes new research on spaceflight blood clotting

slides.explanation: The International Space Station orbits about 250 miles above Earth. This mission focuses on the subtle ways that living in such a unique environment changes the human body over time.

slides.headline: Spaceflight might change how our blood behaves
slides.explanation: Beyond general health checks, astronauts are specifically investigating how blood flows and clots in microgravity. They are also testing manual piloting skills to see how space travel
Both NASA and Phys.org report on these specific biomedical investigations, confirming that this research is a primary focus for the upcoming mission.

slides.subtitle: Read the full breakdown on Headlinne.

instagram.caption:
The SpaceX Crew-13 mission is heading to the International Space Station with a heavy research agenda.

While we often think of space missions in terms of rockets and orbits, the human element remains the most complex variable.

NASA is using this opportunity to study how the body adapts to life without gravity. This includes monitoring blood flow and clotting, which are critical factors for long-term space travel.

They are also testing manual piloting skills during the mission. It is a practical look at how the body maintains performance in a weightless environment.

story_card.headline: UK food and drink trade gap hits record high
story_card.standfirst: The country is importing far more food than it sells abroad, nearing levels not seen

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: The UK's food and drink trade deficit has reached £21 billion. This is the largest gap since 2000.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Brexit, war in the Middle East, and US tariffs hurt exports. Meanwhile, import costs have soared.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Industry leaders worry about food security. They are asking the government to protect local produce.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Look for government policy changes aimed at supporting homegrown food production.

story_card.caption:
The UK food and drink trade deficit has reached its highest point since the year 2000.

Britain is currently spending £21 billion more on food imports than it earns from selling goods abroad. Industry experts are urging ministers to prioritize domestic production to ensure national security remains stable.

Do you think the government should prioritize local food production even if it costs more?
